why: gcd(i, j) > t means i and j share some divisor d > t, so every edge is explained by 'both are multiples of the same d > t'. Uniting all multiples of each d from t+1 to n with union-find builds exactly the components, in harmonic-series time.
hints: Checking all pairs is 2*10^10 gcd calls. If gcd(i, j) = g > t, what do i and j have in common with g?
Both i and j are multiples of g. Conversely all multiples of any d > t are pairwise connected through d. So for each d > t, union d with 2d, 3d, ... up to n.
Union-find with path compression and union by size. Total unions are sum n/d = O(n log n). Then count roots and the largest size.
pitfalls: t = 0 makes everything one component (gcd >= 1 > 0), as in example 2.
t >= n/2 leaves every node isolated, since no d > t has a second multiple <= n.
Start multiples at 2d: a node is already in its own set.
